title: Integrated modelling of crop production and nitrate leaching with the Daisy model
author: Manevski, Børgesen, et al.

steps.title: Collect required input data
steps.instruction: Gather daily weather, soil, crop, and management information needed for Daisy.

steps.title: Create weather input file
steps.instruction: Compile daily air temperature, precipitation, solar radiation, wind speed, and relative humidity recorded at Luancheng station; approximate wet deposition of 7.5 ppm ammonium and 10 kg N ha⁻¹, and dry deposition of 2.5 ppm nitrate and 5 kg N ha⁻¹ from Zhang et al., unless measured values are available.

steps.title: Prepare soil input files
steps.instruction: For each field, construct a soil file using measured soil properties; obtain van Genuchten‑Mualem hydraulic parameters optimized against 2007 water‑retention data in field A with the RETC code and apply these parameters to both fields; discretise the soil column with 2 cm increments from 0–60 cm, 5 cm from 60–170 cm, and 10 cm from 170–210 cm.

steps.title: Select crop parameter files
steps.instruction: Use the Daisy library files ‘Pioneer maize’ for maize and ‘Winter wheat’ for winter wheat, as they provide simulated dry matter dynamics close to measurements.

steps.title: Assemble management file
steps.instruction: Enter the daily management practices recorded for each field during data collection into the Daisy management file.

steps.title: Run baseline Daisy simulation
steps.instruction: Execute Daisy for the N400 treatment in field A using the actual climate record 2000–2013 together with the prepared soil, crop, and management files.

steps.title: Perform mono‑factor sensitivity tests
steps.instruction: For each key parameter related to crop development, leaf photosynthesis, or top‑soil net mineralisation, modify the parameter by +10 % and –10 % while keeping all other inputs at baseline; run the model for each variation and record crop yield and nitrate leaching.

steps.title: Test interacting parameter effects
steps.instruction: Assess crop‑yield sensitivity to selected soil‑parameter changes and nitrate‑leaching sensitivity to selected crop‑parameter changes by repeating the ±10 % perturbations.

steps.title: Interpret sensitivity outcomes
steps.instruction: Note that low crop‑production sensitivity to soil parameters may arise from ample nitrate (except N0); to gain deeper insight, include additional nitrate‑ or soil‑water‑limited treatments when available.
